# Usability Checklist: PB Installer for Linux

**Purpose**: Check that the usability requirements of the guided graphical assistant and the command line are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before planning.
**Created**: 2026-10-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: requirements only (spec.md; constitution Principles IV and V). Depth: formal pre-plan gate. Audience: author and reviewer. There is no plan.md yet, so items that need a design decision are marked `[Gap]`. Install safety is in [install-safety.md](install-safety.md) and security in [security.md](security.md); items here concern what the user sees, is asked and is told. The spec contains no requirement on progress, cancelling or accessibility at all, so those groups are mostly `[Gap]` items.

## Finding the Reader and Choosing a Folder

- [x] CHK001 Is it specified how the program finds a reader on start (a scan once, or watching for a reader that appears later), and what the user sees while no reader has been found yet? [Gap, Spec §FR-001, §US1 scenario 1]
- [x] CHK002 Is the information shown for each candidate drive defined (volume label, mount point, size, and what else) so that two similar readers can be told apart, and is the same information required in both front ends? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases "Several readers or drives"]
- [x] CHK003 Is the manual choice of a folder defined for both front ends (how it is chosen, and that the same acceptability test as for an automatically found drive runs before anything else), including what the user sees when the folder fails the test? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §US1 scenario 6]
- [x] CHK004 Is behavior defined when the reader is unplugged, or a second one is plugged in, while the program is open and idle, or after a plan has been shown but before it is confirmed? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK005 Is it defined when the reader's contents are read (once at the start or again before each plan), and what happens when the contents changed between the plan and the confirmation? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK006 Is it specified how the program starts with no arguments and no graphical session (assistant, command-line help, or an error), and how a user chooses between the two front ends? [Gap, Spec §FR-028]

## Refusing Wrong Drives and Unwritable Storage

- [x] CHK007 Does every refusal (not a reader, MTP or charge-only, read-only, no write rights, not enough space) state which expected part is missing or what is wrong, and what the user can do next, in the same wording in both front ends? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-030]
- [x] CHK008 Is the guidance for a reader that shows as MTP or charge-only specific enough to follow (what to select on the reader's connection prompt, and that the program waits or must be started again)? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases "Reader shows as MTP"]
- [x] CHK009 Is it defined what the user can still do after a refusal (try again, choose another folder, view what is installed, install from a local file) so that a refusal is never a dead end? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases "No reader found", "No network"]

## The App List and the States

- [x] CHK010 Is the information shown for each app in the list defined (name, installed version, offered version, state, source, short description), and the order of the list? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020, §US1 scenario 1]
- [x] CHK011 Are the four states defined in user wording, each with the actions it offers (install, update, remove, adopt, replace), and is it clear what a user can do with an app in each state? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020, §US5]
- [x] CHK012 Is "installed outside the installer" explained to the user in plain words (what the program saw, why it cannot treat the app as its own, what replacing it would change, and that the user's data is not touched), instead of only being a label? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-023, §US5 scenario 2]
- [x] CHK013 Is the difference between "installed outside the installer" and the notes "installed from a local file" and "no longer in the catalog" explained, and is it defined which of these can be removed (an app without an install record cannot)? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-020, §Key Entities "App State"]
- [x] CHK014 Is adoption described to the user as an action with a name, a result and an explanation ("records it, changes nothing else"), and is the word used consistently ("adopt", "record")? [Consistency, Spec §FR-023, §US5]
- [x] CHK015 Is the empty state defined (a catalog with no offered app, or no app installed on the reader), and the state of an app whose offered version is withdrawn, so the list never looks broken? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK016 Is the display of the catalog's age and of the "not from the catalog, not signed by the maintainer" marking defined for the list, the plan and the result, with the same wording each time? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, §FR-025]

## The Plan and the Confirmations

- [x] CHK017 Is the content and form of a plan defined for each action (install, update, remove, adopt, replace, repair, local install) so that "exactly what it will write" is the same list for every action? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK018 Is it defined how a long plan (hundreds of files) is shown in the assistant and on the command line (summary with a way to see all files, or all of it)? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK019 Are all the extra confirmations listed in one place (edited recorded files, unknown firmware version, existing data folder, replacing an app outside the installer, repair, data folder deletion twice), each with the wording it must carry? [Completeness, Consistency, Spec §FR-018, §FR-021, §FR-022, §FR-023, §FR-026]
- [x] CHK020 Is it clear for each confirmation what the default answer is and that the safe answer is the default (decline) in the assistant, and that the command line never answers on the user's behalf? [Clarity, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK021 Is a single confirmation step required to cover a plan with several warnings, or must each warning be answered on its own, and is that the same in both front ends? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011, §FR-026]
- [x] CHK022 Is the second of the two data-folder deletion confirmations required to differ from the first in wording and position, so that it is not answered by habit? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021]

## Progress and Cancel

- [x] CHK023 Are progress requirements defined for the steps that take time (download of up to 64 MiB, checks, copy to a slow USB volume), including what the user sees when a step has no measurable progress? [Gap, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK024 Is cancelling defined for each phase: before the confirmation (nothing written), during the download, and during the write? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK025 Is it stated what cancelling or closing the window during a write does (finish, undo, or refuse to cancel), and is it consistent with the interrupted-operation rules (an interruption by the user is the same as one by a pulled cable)? [Consistency, Gap, Spec §FR-018, §US2]
- [x] CHK026 Is the command line's handling of an interrupt from the keyboard defined with the same rules as cancelling in the assistant? [Consistency, Gap, Spec §FR-028]
- [x] CHK027 Is a hang defined: a network step that stalls, or a reader that stops responding, with a limit after which the user is told? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §Edge Cases "No network"]

## After the Action: Eject and Restart

- [x] CHK028 Is the final message after an install, update or removal specified (what was done, what the user must do next, where the app will appear), with the same content in both front ends? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, §US1 scenario 4]
- [x] CHK029 Is "ejected safely" turned into steps a user can follow on a Linux desktop, and is it decided whether the program offers to flush or unmount the drive itself? [Ambiguity, Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK030 Is the wording "a restart may be needed" fixed, with the way the user can tell whether it was needed, and is it required after removal as well as after install and update? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019, §Clarifications]
- [x] CHK031 Is the statement of where the app will appear specified for all cases (group name and title; an app whose menu entry only shows after a restart), and is anything said about the app's data folder, which stays after removal? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, §FR-021]

## Plain Messages

- [x] CHK032 Is a message structure defined (what happened, whether the reader changed, what to do next, the rule id) and used for every failure class, not only those listed in the edge cases? [Completeness, Spec §FR-030, §SC-009]
- [x] CHK033 Is it defined how several findings from one package are reported (all of them or the first one), and in what order? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-030]
- [x] CHK034 Is the place for technical details defined (the log, a details area), so that a plain message can be read by anyone while the details remain available, and so that "no stack traces alone" is checkable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-030, §FR-031]
- [x] CHK035 Are the messages for "the reader was changed" cases defined too (a failure that needed an undo, a recovery that could not finish), not only for failures that leave the reader unchanged? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-030, §FR-018]
- [x] CHK036 Is a glossary of the user-facing terms defined (reader, app, package, catalog, installed outside the installer, adopt, repair, data folder) so that both front ends, the log and the documentation use one word for each thing? [Consistency, Gap, Spec §Key Entities]

## Dry Run

- [x] CHK037 Is the dry run defined for the assistant as well as for the command line (how a user asks for it, and how a dry-run result is told apart from a real one)? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK038 Is the claim that a dry run prints "the same plan" reconciled with steps that need the network and a download, and is it stated whether a dry run downloads and checks the package? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012, §US7 scenario 2]

## Command Line: Options, Output and Exit Codes

- [x] CHK039 Is the set of commands and options defined at requirements level (actions, how the folder is named, how each confirmation is given, how a local package is named, dry run), with one option per confirmation rather than a single "yes to all"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK040 Are the exit statuses defined beyond three classes: declined by the user, nothing to do, a repair needed and not confirmed, cancelled, partly done and recovered, and is the relation to the existing catalog tool's `0/1/2` convention stated? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-029, §US8 scenario 3, docs/contracts/cli.md]
- [x] CHK041 Is the output split defined (plan and result on standard output, findings on the error output), and the line format of a finding specified in the same form the contract uses (`error[<rule id>] <subject>: <message>`)? [Consistency, Gap, Spec §US8, docs/contracts/cli.md]
- [x] CHK042 Is a stable, machine-readable output for scripts and tests either required or deliberately excluded, given that "for scripting and for the tests" is the stated purpose of the command line? [Gap, Spec §FR-029, §FR-028]
- [x] CHK043 Is the behavior without a terminal defined (a prompt that cannot be answered): stop with a message, never wait forever, never assume an answer? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK044 Is a way to see what the program knows without risk (list of apps, what is installed) defined for the command line with the same content as in the assistant? [Completeness, Spec §US7 scenario 1]

## Both Front Ends Together

- [x] CHK045 Is "same steps, same results" made checkable by saying what must be identical (the order of steps, the plan text, the final message, the reader contents) and what may differ (layout, prompts)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-028, §SC-007]
- [x] CHK046 Are accessibility needs addressed or deliberately excluded for the assistant (use by keyboard alone, readable text size, not relying on colour), given an audience of ordinary users? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK047 Is the format of sizes, dates and counts in messages fixed (units such as MiB, date style), consistent with the English-only decision? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions "Languages"]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK048 Is SC-001 ("a user who has never used the program ... under 3 minutes") defined well enough to measure: who the test users are, which task (including finding the reader), where the clock starts and stops? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK049 Does the success criteria cover the user-facing requirements of this checklist (cancel, progress, messages for every refusal, the post-action message) with a measurable condition, instead of only SC-009 for messages? [Coverage, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK050 Does each user-facing requirement (FR-001, FR-011, FR-012, FR-019, FR-020, FR-028 to FR-030) map to at least one acceptance scenario that can be checked in both front ends? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements, §User Scenarios]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Largest gaps (no requirement exists at all): progress and cancel (CHK023 to CHK027), accessibility (CHK046), the list of commands and options (CHK039), exit statuses beyond three classes (CHK040), what happens when the reader changes between plan and confirmation (CHK005), and what "eject safely" means to the user on Linux (CHK029)
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference; numbering starts again at CHK001 in each checklist file
